$comment: HIPAA (45 CFR Part 164) → ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A control mappings. Derived from the primary CFR text cross-walked against Annex A control intent, informed by the publicly available NIST SP 800-66r2 crosswalk appendix (HIPAA Security Rule ↔ NIST CSF ↔ ISO). HIPAA safeguards are organisational obligations that are usually broader than a single Annex A control, so 'partial' dominates; 'equivalent' is reserved for genuine 1:1 intent.
source: 45 CFR Part 164 cross-walk informed by NIST SP 800-66r2 mapping appendix

mappings.rationale: Both require a disciplinary/sanction process for workforce security violations.
System-activity review presumes the audit logs that A.8.15 requires.
Regular review of activity records is the monitoring activity A.8.16 formalises.
Naming a Security Official is a specific instance of defining security roles and responsibilities.
Workforce clearance before ePHI access aligns with pre-employment screening.
Termination procedures cover post-employment security responsibilities.
Removing leaver access is the revocation half of access-rights management.
Granting ePHI access under documented policy is core access control.
Establishing, reviewing and modifying user access rights is the same lifecycle A.5.18 governs.
Periodic security reminders are one delivery channel of an awareness programme.
Guarding against and detecting malicious software maps to anti-malware protection.
Password creation, change and safeguarding procedures are authentication-information management.
Both require planned, documented incident-management procedures.
Responding to and mitigating incidents matches incident response; HIPAA adds ePHI-specific documentation duties.
Identifying suspected incidents relies on a workforce event-reporting channel.
Retrievable exact copies of ePHI are the information backups A.8.13 requires.
Restoring lost ePHI is the ICT-readiness outcome of business-continuity planning.
Emergency-mode operation preserves security of information during disruption.
Contingency-plan testing evidences ICT continuity readiness.
Periodic technical/nontechnical evaluation parallels independent review of information security.
Evaluation against the Security Rule is compliance checking against policies and standards.
Obtaining assurances from business associates is supplier-relationship security.
BAAs put the required security terms into supplier agreements.
A facility security plan defines the physical security perimeter and its safeguards.
Role-based facility access with visitor control is physical-entry control.
Workstation-use rules govern user endpoint devices handling ePHI.
Physical workstation safeguards overlap clear-desk/clear-screen and positioning controls.
Both require secure disposal of equipment and media holding sensitive data.
Sanitising media before re-use is part of storage-media lifecycle management.
Tracking media movements and custodians is storage-media handling control.
Unique user identifiers are the foundation of identity management.
Automatic logoff supports the clear-screen objective for unattended sessions.
Encrypting stored ePHI is an application of the cryptography control.
Recording and examining activity in ePHI systems is the logging control's exact intent.
Verifying the identity of persons/entities seeking ePHI is secure authentication.
Protecting ePHI during electronic transfer is information-transfer security.
Encrypting ePHI in transit applies the cryptography control to transmission.
Mandatory BAA security clauses are supplier-agreement security requirements.
Written security policies and operational records align with documented operating procedures.
Six-year retention and availability of compliance documentation is records protection.
Individual breach notification is executed through the incident-response process, but the 60-day duty is HIPAA-specific.
Minimum-necessary use of PHI supports the privacy/PII-protection control.
The notice of privacy practices is a transparency measure for PII processing.
Individual access rights are operationalised within PII privacy controls.
Privacy-programme administration (official, training, safeguards) underpins PII protection.
